articles.title: La UFC actualiza su ránking libra por libra e Ilia Topuria no cambia de puesto
articles.summary: El 'Matador' se mantiene quinto
articles.body: Nueva actualización del ránking libra por libra tras la celebración de UFC 331 y la consolidación de Joshua Van (18-2) como una de las grandes estrellas jóvenes de la compañía. El campeón del peso mosca, de hecho, protagoniza el gran 'subidón' de este mes... mientras que Ilia Topuria (17-1) mantiene el quinto puesto mientras espera su retorno. Joshua Van ha sido el gran beneficiado de una semana con cambios en el ránking libra por libra. El birmano, segundo campeón más joven de la historia de la UFC tras Jon Jones, derrotó a Pantoja en su segunda defensa del título del peso mosca... y sube al sexto puesto. También asciende Justin Gaethje (28-5)... sin pelear. El estadounidense, que derrotó a Topuria en UFC Casa Blanca el pasado mes de junio, es TOP-3 y adelanta al ruso Petr Yan (20-5) ante de la pelea del europeo el próximo mes de noviembre, en Abu Dhabi. Sube Arman Tsarukyan (23-4) después de su espectacular victoria sobre Ruffy este pasado fin de semana... y entra Carlos Ulberg (14-1) mientras se recupera de su lesión pero mantiene su corona del peso semi-pesado de la UFC.

articles.title: Movsar Evloev reacts to UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski backing him for title shot ahead of UFC 333 showdown
articles.summary: Movsar Evloev has shown major respect for Alexander Volkanovski ahead of their UFC 333 featherweight title fight.
articles.body: Movsar Evloev has shown major respect for Alexander Volkanovski ahead of their UFC 333 featherweight title fight. The undefeated Russian contender praised Volkanovski for repeatedly supporting his case for a championship opportunity and called the Australian a genuine champion.Evloev believes Volkanovski’s backing was sincere and showed that the champion respects the best fighters in the division. The two will now settle their rivalry inside the Octagon in Abu Dhabi on October 24, 2026.Movsar Evloev calls Alexander Volkanovski “the real one” after title-shot supportMovsar Evloev’s journey to a UFC featherweight title opportunity has not been straightforward. The undefeated fighter has dealt with several cancelled and postponed bouts during his UFC career.Despite those setbacks, Evloev believes he is challenging for the title at the right time. He has remained unbeaten and continued to build his record while waiting for his opportunity.Volkanovski’s support has been an important part of the story. The Australian champion has repeatedly acknowledged Evloev’s unbeaten record and credentials. He has also backed the Russian’s claim to fight for the belt.Evloev clearly appreciated that support.“Volk is not fake. He’s the real one. He’s the champ, and he deserves to be there, and I do too”, he said via MMA Fighting.The comments show the level of respect Evloev has for the reigning champion. Rather than treating Volkanovski’s support as simple promotion, Evloev believes it came from genuine respect.The two fighters will now meet with the UFC featherweight championship on the line. Volkanovski will defend his title against Evloev in the main event of UFC 333 at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi.For Evloev, the fight represents the biggest opportunity of his career.The Russian enters the contest with an unbeaten professional record of 20-0. His wrestling and grappling have been major parts of his success. He has consistently used his control and takedowns to frustrate opponents and win decisions.However, Evloev has also suggested that he is prepared to stand and trade if Volkanovski wants to make the fight a striking contest.“For this camp, we do everything we’re ready to do striking match, as he said he’s going to make this fight a striking match. Okay, in this case we’re ready for striking too,” Evloev said.Volkanovski, meanwhile, brings extensive championship experience into the matchup. The Australian has established himself as one of the leading fighters of his generation and has also worked on his grappling ahead of the challenge.Evloev’s path to the title has included several frustrating interruptions. A positive COVID-19 test forced him out of his planned fight against Ilia Topuria at UFC 270 in 2022. Other bouts were also cancelled after opponents suffered injuries.More recently, illness forced him out of a scheduled fight with Aaron Pico. articles.standfirst: Merab Dvalishvili habla sobre su amigo Ilia Topuria
articles.summary: Merab Dvalishvili habla sobre su amigo Ilia Topuria
articles.body: El futuro de Ilia Topuria (17-1) está por escribir. Mientras el 'Matador' sigue con su recuperación y espera la decisión de UFC de cara a su próximo combate, en el que aspira a enfrentarse de nuevo a Justin Gaethje (28-5) para recuperar el cinturón del peso ligero, diferentes nombres dentro de la compañía se pronuncian. Y uno de los que mejor conoce al doble campeón hispanogeorgiano ha hablado: Merab Dvalishvili (21-5). El ex campeón del peso gallo, que buscará recuperar su cetro en noviembre ante Petr Yan, ha hablado en el canal del streamer 'N30n'. "Creo que Gaethje debería conceder la revancha a Topuria. Ilia fue campeón y se merece esa revancha", afirma el georgiano. Las incógnitas, no obstante, son muchas: no está claro que Gaethje vaya a defender su título y vuelva a pelear... y nombres como el de Arman Tsarukyan (24-3), que viene de arrasar a Ruffy en UFC 331, cotizan al alza de cara a poder pelear por el título. articles.title: Coach: Francis Ngannou could be 'greatest ever to do it' if he sticks to MMA
articles.summary: Eric Nicksick thinks Francis Ngannou has a lot more to give in MMA.
articles.body:
Eric Nicksick thinks Francis Ngannou has a lot more to give in MMA.

Ngannou has been competing in MMA and boxing simultaneously ever since parting ways with the UFC in 2022. The former UFC heavyweight champion is coming off back-to-back first-round knockouts of Renan Ferreira and Philipe Lins in MMA.

Nicksick isn't sure what's next for Ngannou (19-3), but plans on finding out very soon.

"I'll actually see him in a couple of days," Nicksick told MMA Junkie Radio. "... He hasn't really said much about anything. He celebrated his 40th birthday at the beginning of the month and he had a pretty big blowout, so we'll see. I'll get caught up with him and see what's on his mind, and what he wants to do from a boxing standpoint or MMA standpoint. Hopefully MMA, because obviously I think we're making some really good strides there. But we'll see what MVP has to offer for him."

While the bigger opportunities have come in the ring, where Ngannou boxed both Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua, Nicksick wants "The Predator" to continue being undeniable in MMA.

"For me personally, the boxing side of things is very much a learning experience for me," Nicksick said. "I use that time to really sit back and watch what Dewey (Cooper) does and the other coaches and learn how to kind of formulate a game plan when it comes to something that I'm not very familiar with. But on the MMA side of things, we've talked about this for years, man.

"Just the development of Francis from that Jairzinho fight all the way to Ciryl Gane to now. it's like, man, there's so many things that we're advancing on. I just wish we had more time in the MMA space because I feel like we could break a lot of records, and he could be left as the greatest ever to do it. And that's just having more time in the cage. So that's where I think selfishly, I would love to see him fight more MMA."
authors: Farah Hannoun, George Garcia and Brian Garcia, MMA Junkie

articles.title: Oktagon just debunked a Dana White myth to show MMA’s true potential
articles.summary: IN FOCUS: European promotion Oktagon is making MMA in a football stadium fashionable, writes Will Castle in Frankfurt, and the UFC is missing a trick
articles.body:
Dana White doesn't like stadium shows. His UFC will never do one. "Nothing will change my mind about a stadium show," White asserted in April 2025. "I am not a fan of stadiums. I like arenas."

He puts his disdain of open-air fight cards down to a lack of atmosphere. Apparently, fans can't make enough noise when not in a closed system.

On Saturday, one European MMA promotion debunked such a myth. Again.

Enter Oktagon. Primarily based in Germany, Slovakia and the Czech Republic, it is very much a regional brand to the UFC's global juggernaut. Yet for the second time in three years, the company has blown White and co out of the water.

In October 2024, Oktagon broke the record for the most-attended MMA show (outside of a couple early-2000s Pride events in Japan) when it welcomed nearly 60,000 fans to Deutsche Bank Park, the home of Bundesliga club Eintracht Frankfurt . Two years on, the company returned for Oktagon 94 trying to go bigger and better.

It could only achieve one or the other. Co-founder Pavol Neruda admitted he had to sacrifice breaking his own attendance record for the sake of the spectacle, chiefly a huge entrance stage which would also become the focal point of one of Oktagon's USPs: a half-time show. Fronted by diamond-selling artist Robin Schulz, what could have easily detracted from the event if done wrong actually proved a hit.

The only downside to the half-time show was that many of the continental fans, likely still baulking at the concept after the abomination we got at the World Cup final, used the musical interlude as their toilet break. There were more empty seats here than at any other point on the seven-hour card. Though that speaks to a different point about the Oktagon faithful.

From the second prelim onwards, the stadium was near-full. Hearing what Michael Obodozie did in the opener – knocking his opponent down, celebrating on the cage, getting told by the referee the fight wasn't over, climbing down before promptly finishing the job, all in one minute and four seconds – may have got any stragglers in the fan zone to sink their pints.

That sort of early turnout is unheard of in the UFC, or any marquee boxing event for that matter. The appreciation of fighting in these parts is like no other, and it's why Oktagon has been able to achieve these heights in just 10 years of existence. "The demand is growing here in Germany. That's what we want to use," Neruda told The Independent .

The action lived up to the occasion. Seven finishes in 10 fights, six in the first round, speaks for itself. The noise was indeed deafening despite White's contention, especially for local heroes Max Coga and Christian Eckerlin, who experienced opposite fortunes in the final two fights. Coga's arm was raised after a barn-burner co-main event with Christian Jungwirth, while Eckerlin was submitted by former champion David Kozma with two seconds left of the headliner's first round amid talk of retirement.

The night didn't exactly go off without a hitch, however, with Oktagon suffering an untimely power cut mid-fight during a featherweight prelim bout between Deniz Ilbay and Hugo Vach. The cage lost its illumination for around two minutes, forcing the fight to be paused. Eardrum-bursting whistles from all four stands ensued.

For a brief period, the worst fears had come true. Sources say Oktagon flagged a potential issue with power supply to Deutsche Bank Park organisers before the event but the necessary improvements weren't made in time. The unprecedented outage left Oktagon personnel scrambling, unsure if power would come back on. Fortunately it did – and moments later, underdog Ilbay knocked Vach out with one devastating right, the second instance of lights out in quick succession.

Ilbay cited his dad's "crazy" training exercises – such as putting a cover over his head while sparring – as the reason why he was able to lock in despite the outage. Vach meanwhile lamented the malfunction for derailing his momentum but insisted: "I don't want to make excuses."

This event did feel like it was about more than fighting. Oktagon came to Frankfurt at a tumultuous time, with protests in the left-leaning city rife amid election success for far-right party AfD in Germany. There was a demonstration in the city centre on the day of the fight. Neruda, perhaps not wanting to alienate any of his fanbase, claimed he was unaware of the political situation – but hailed the power of the sport in "connecting people and destroying boundaries". And it did feel like 58,000 came together for a common cause, for the love of the game.

The biggest MMA event of the year in terms of significance will still go down as the UFC's White House card. That's something even Neruda recognises: "No doubt." But for all the presidential glamour, there was one glaring thing missing on the South Lawn: atmosphere.

It's ironic, given atmosphere lies at the root of White's aversion to stadium shows. But the UFC's loss is Oktagon's gain, who now plan to do this yearly ; this is not a cost-sapping one-time novelty, unlike UFC Freedom 250.

"We want to say to Europe and even to the world that we are here. We are doing something special, and it's worth the watch," Neruda says. Statement made.

articles.title: Jake Paul's MVP breaks silence on $10 million lawsuit over Hardy's fight injury
articles.summary: Jake Paul’s MVP [Most Valuable Promotions] has finally addressed boxing legend Heather Hardy’s $10 million lawsuit. Hardy, 44, suffered several injuries thro...
articles.body:
Jake Paul 's MVP [Most Valuable Promotions] has finally addressed boxing legend Heather Hardy's $10 million lawsuit. Hardy, 44, suffered several injuries throughout her career but finished her professional career with a loss against Amanda Serrano.

The Heather-Serrano fight co-main evented the Jake Paul vs. Nate Diaz at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas in 2023. Hardy was beaten by Serrano in 2019, and the same outcome was repeated four years later.

However, Hardy recently initiated a lawsuit in the U.S. District Court of Northern Texas, citing alleged violations of the Muhammad Ali Reform Act due to negligence. She claimed that the organisers ignored potential red flags during her fight and ensured the energetic fight advanced. She further suggested that the fight gave her a career-ending brain injury. She also noted that she suffered "permanent brain injury" during the loss.

Now, in a recent statement to ESPN, Jake Paul's MVP has broken their silence on the matter. "MVP has great respect for Heather Hardy. We recognize the difficulty of her circumstances and extend our sincere sympathy and hope that she receives the care and support she deserves.

"Heather's participation on our August 5, 2023 card was arranged through her promoter, Lou DiBella, who contracted for the fight, and Heather publicly expressed her gratitude for the opportunity both before and after the fight," quotes available as per ESPN.

"MVP followed applicable protocols for the fight, Heather was medically cleared to compete by the athletic commission overseeing the event, and the bout proceeded under the commission's authority and supervision in accordance with their standard medical and safety requirements. MVP remains committed to fighter safety and supporting the athletes who compete in our events in full compliance with commission standards."

A women's boxing legend, Hardy has fought around 27 professional boxing matches, where she secured a total of 24 wins and three losses. A former pro-boxer, Hardy has also participated in MMA events, namely for Bellator.

articles.title: Una excampeona demanda a la promotora de Jake Paul por 10 millones debido a las lesiones cerebrales sufridas
articles.standfirst: Heather Hardy demanda a la promotora Most Valuable Promotions
articles.summary: Heather Hardy demanda a la promotora Most Valuable Promotions
articles.body: Este verano, la excampeona mundial Heather Hardy (44 años), retirada en 2024, reveló que sufre una lesión cerebral traumática como consecuencia de los golpes recibidos durante su carrera. Dicho anuncio fue acompañado de la creación de una campaña en GoFundMe para recaudar fondos para ella y su hija. “Después de años recibiendo golpes por el deporte que amaba, sufrí una lesión cerebral traumática. El daño ha afectado a mi salud, mi visión y mi capacidad para trabajar con suficiente regularidad como para cubrir los gastos básicos”, explicó la expúgil. El momento culminante de su carrera llegó en octubre de 2018, cuando derrotó por decisión unánime a Shelly Vincent y conquistó el título mundial de la WBO del peso pluma. En su siguiente pelea (2019) se enfrentaría a Amanda Serrano, con quien perdería por decisión unánime. En realidad entre 2019 y 2023 sólo combatiría cinco veces, siendo la última una revancha contra Serrano en agosto de 2023. Meses después, en mayo de 2024, anunció que no continuaría compitiendo de acuerdo a las recomendaciones médicas recibidas. El caso es que ahora Hardy ha demandado por 10 millones de dólares a Most Valuable Promotions (MVP), la promotora cuya cara visible es Jake Paul, bajo cuyo paraguas peleó por última vez contra Serrano. Por aquel combate, la boxeadora neoyorkina cobró la mayor bolsa de su carrera. La demanda que ha presentado tiene que ver con presuntas infracciones de la Ley de Reforma Muhammad Ali por negligencia. Hardy afirma que los organizadores ignoraron las posibles señales de alerta respecto a su estado de salud y se aseguraron de que el combate siguiera adelante, aprovechando además su delicada situación financiera para presionarla. La boxeadora sostiene que dicho evento le provocó una "lesión cerebral que pone fin a su carrera”, con repercusiones que van más allá de una carrera deportiva. En un comunicado, Most Valuable Promotions ha expresado su respeto por Hardy, pero no se consideran causantes de los problemas de salud que esta haya podido tener. "La participación de Heather en nuestra cartelera del 5 de agosto de 2023 se gestionó a través de su promotor, Lou DiBella, quien contrató la pelea, y Heather expresó públicamente su gratitud por la oportunidad tanto antes como después del combate. MVP siguió los protocolos aplicables para la pelea, Heather recibió la autorización médica para competir por parte de la comisión atlética que supervisaba el evento, y el combate se desarrolló bajo la autoridad y supervisión de la comisión de acuerdo con sus requisitos médicos y de seguridad estándar", explican.

articles.title: Abdelkrim Zouad, en busca del cinturón de PFL Mena: "Ese título va a venir a España"
articles.standfirst: El peleador del Barcelona MMA Team se medirá este viernes a Omar Hussein con la intención de meterse en las finales del torneo de peso ligero y acercarse a su sueño
articles.summary: El peleador del Barcelona MMA Team se medirá este viernes a Omar Hussein con la intención de meterse en las finales del torneo de peso ligero y acercarse a su sueño
articles.body: Este viernes 2 de octubre está marcado en rojo en el calendario de Abdelkrim Zouad (8-2), que se medirá a Omar Hussein (12-7) con el objetivo de sellar su pase a las finales de PFL Mena del torneo de peso ligero y dar un paso de gigante en su carrera. MARCA ha podido charlar con el peleador argelino del 'Barcelona MMA Team' en los días previos al combate, en una entrevista que ha servido para conocer sus inicios, una mentalidad a la altura de unos pocos elegidos y una ambición que no tiene límites. P. Hola, ¿cómo lleva la preparación de cara a una pelea tan importante? R. La verdad, muy, muy bien, pero ya sabemos que el corte de peso es jodido. Pero bueno vamos a por ello y con muchas ganas de llevarme la victoria. P. ¿Cómo llega a España y cómo se inicia en los deportes de contacto? R. Entreno en el Barcelona MMA Team. Llegué aquí y empecé en boxeo. Luego nos cambiaron el gimnasio, nos llevaron a No Limits, y ahí estaba Rai, con el equipo MMA Barcelona. Les dije que tenía base de suelo, porque empecé jiu-jitsu en Argelia, y me dio la oportunidad de demostrar mi nivel de grappling y todo. También hacía judo en Argelia, hacía muchas disciplinas desde pequeño. Me dio la oportunidad de demostrar lo que sé. A España vine por el campeonato del mundo en Portugal, de grappling. Mi entrenador de Argelia me dijo, si quieres tener futuro, tienes que quedarte aquí en Europa, porque en Argelia no había MMA. Yo, desde pequeño, mi objetivo y el de mi padre era ser el mejor luchador de MMA. Fui a Francia, porque como soy argelino tengo familia y todo, pero no había suerte. Desde ahí cogí un tren y vine aquí a Barcelona, no tenía a nadie aquí y no sabía decir ni hola. Y ahora, gracias a Dios, tengo familia, tengo mi mujer, tengo todo. Vivía en Tarragona, y vine hasta Barcelona para entrenar, cada día. Si quieres algo, lo vas a lograr. Sigo así, hoy o mañana. Si quieres, puedes. Me siento orgulloso de donde estoy, de la forma en que estoy peleando, pero aún hay que trabajar más, hay que seguir. P. ¿Perdió en su debut profesional. ¿Cómo vivió aquello? R. Fue muy difícil, ahí me agobié mucho. No lo acepté. Yo soy muy competitivo. Me enfermé, y como vivía solo lo pasé muy mal. Después de eso estuve casi dos años sin competir, sin entrenar MMA, sin nada. No era profesional, estaba perdido. Era un buen amateur, pero subí a profesional y me hacían técnicas que yo ni sabía cómo defender. Tenía que pasar lo que pasó y, como dices, la flecha fue hacia atrás para volver más fuerte. Desde ahí aprendí mucho. No perdí, aprendí, eso sí. P. De hecho, después de eso llegaron siete victorias y seis finalizaciones... R. Me sentí muy orgulloso en ese momento. Aún no llegué donde quiero llegar, la verdad. Mi objetivo es muy grande. Es tan grande que me da miedo a veces. Así que tengo que luchar y tengo que entrenar y ser más disciplinado y seguir. P. Antes de dar el salto a PFL sufre su segunda derrota, esta vez por K.O. que no le había pasado antes. ¿Cómo se repuso de ese mazazo? R. Fue muy difícil el combate que perdí por KO en el primer round porque estaba a un paso de una liga muy grande. Lo pasé muy mal el día del corte del peso, lo pasé demasiado mal. Cometí el error de seguir. Decía, '¿qué va a pasar? No va a pasar nada'. Me quedó la espina clavada de no poder demostrar mi nivel de verdad. Si me gana como mi debut, que fue mejor que yo, te duele, pero lo aceptas. Pero cuando no puedes ni te da la oportunidad de demostrar lo que sabes, lo que tienes, de golpe siete victorias y de golpe derrota el primer round, no sé, el primer minuto, fue muy duro. Estoy también agradecido porque he vuelto a entrenar y he vuelto a ganar. La verdad, no ha sido fácil. Es la otra cara de la moneda. Es muy difícil, es una vida muy dura. Puedes volverte loco, pero es lo que hay, hay que ser luchador dentro y fuera de la jaula y tener fe. Gracias a Dios por la gente que tengo alrededor, mi equipo, mi familia, mi mujer, me ayudaron demasiado, sobre todo Dios. No puedes vencer a un hombre que está luchando por su familia. No tengo plan B, ni quiero tenerlo. Yo tengo ese plan y lo voy a lograr. No hay otra, no tengo otra salida. Ese título es mío, hasta ellos saben que es mío ese título. No sé por qué están ahí cortando peso, entrenando cada día. De verdad, no estoy ofendiendo a nadie, pero ese título va a venir a España. Voy a ganarles a todos porque estoy bien preparado, estoy bajando muy bien el peso, estoy haciendo las cosas gracias a Dios bien y gracias a mi equipo. Nada me va a parar ahora. Nada y nadie. P. ¿Esa oportunidad que se escapó era con UFC o Dana White's Contender Series? R. Exacto, pero todo pasa por algo. Se cierra esa puerta y ahora mira. Hay muchas puertas y voy a llevar el título a España. Así que, igual, UFC, PFL... Estoy muy orgulloso de mí y de lo que estoy haciendo. P. Tras esa derrota llega la llamada de PFL para el torneo de PFL Mena y debuta a lo grande con finalización. ¿Cómo recuerda ese día y todo el apoyo recibido a posteriori? R. La verdad es que lo pasé muy mal un día antes de la pelea. Es muy duro volver de una derrota, porque hasta sabes que tu rival te ve como si fueras un paquete. Estaba muy estresado. Después de la victoria me siento muy bien y muy feliz. Es muy importante esta victoria para mí, es muy importante porque gané a un rival también muy fuerte, muy bueno. Me dio mucho esa victoria porque estaba como un puente negro, oscuro, y ya he visto la luz. He visto un poco de luz, así que vamos a seguir hasta que salga más de ese puente. P. ¿Qué opina de la pelea en semifinales ante Omar Hussein y qué espera de él? R. He visto todos sus combates, lo tenemos estudiado. No me gusta hablar mucho, tampoco me gusta así como ser muy confiado. No hay que hablar mucho, todo lo voy a demostrar el 2 de octubre, pero las cosas se hacen bien. He visto sus combates, los estudié mucho junto a todo mi equipo y lo hemos entrenado muy bien. Es un peleador completo, con mucha experiencia, pero lo voy a ganar. Aprendí muchas cosas. La confianza cero, pero trabajo 1000%. P. Más allá del cinturón de PFL Mena, ¿cuál es su hoja de ruta para el futuro? R. Pedro, muchos luchadores quieren ser luchadores profesionales, yo quiero ser el mejor, quiero ser leyenda, quiero ser el mejor del planeta. No hablo así, que hay gente que te vean cuando digas estas cosas, te vean como loco, yo lo hablo de verdad y hablo en serio. Quiero ser el mejor, y voy a demostrarlo. Y después del torneo este, lo dejamos en las manos de Dios, porque me llamó el manager, Pedro Faustino, y me dijo, primero vamos a enfocarnos en el combate que viene, vamos a ganar el título, y ahí sí que nos va a abrir muchas puertas. Así que, tío, vamos a lograrlo, vamos a ganar ese título, y el siguiente paso será grande, estoy segurísimo.

articles.title: Dillian Whyte was suffering from a broken foot in Moses Itauma defeat but wants to return in British battle with Johnny Fisher
articles.summary: Dillian Whyte has revealed that he was suffering from a broken foot in his defeat by Moses Itauma last August; Whyte fractured his foot during his training camp and then injured it again in the changing room; 'The Body Snatcher' wants to return against Johnny Fisher this year
articles.body:
"It felt like someone had dropped a dumbbell on my foot," revealed Whyte when asked to put into words the pain caused by the fractured foot that he sustained in training last summer.

"I was running and I felt it [my foot] and then I went to spar and I was sparring big, agile guys and someone was pressing me, I stepped back the wrong way and then it just fractured clean.

"It was terrible, but we're used to pulling off miracles. We're used to fighting injured.

"I made the best of the situation and had a decent camp. I felt good during fight week and really thought I would beat Moses."

Whyte has entered the ring before with debilitating injuries. He famously fought bitter rival Anthony Joshua whilst being hampered by a badly damaged shoulder and other grim wounds have been overcome in a heavyweight career that led him to become two-time WBC interim world champion.

But the Brixton man could not shrug off the effects of his injured foot and the bone fractured again while he was limbering up in the dressing room, only hours before he was due to face Itauma in Saudi Arabia last August.

"I started warming up, jumped a little bit of rope, and then reinjured the foot. Completely fractured it again," said Whyte.

"We had to call the doctor who was with me to examine it. He advised me not to fight and I said 'no'. There's no way I'm going to come all the way to Saudi and not fight last minute.

"I was confident that I would still be able to drag Moses into the later rounds and stop him as [Filip] Hrgovic recently did."

Whyte tried to conceal his damaged foot, which had been heavily strapped, but his lack of mobility was exposed by Itauma, who piled on a succession of punches before the bout was waved off in the opening round.

While Itauma celebrated his victory, Whyte remained silent about his significant injury and has been absent from the ring since that fight.

"I didn't want to mention it, go into it, and take away from his win, because he done alright. I got clocked and he won the fight.

"I didn't want to go on too much about it and I think people got carried away with the fact that I got beat in a round by Moses.

"I don't think people would draw the same conclusions if they had the full facts.

"People have short memories and they like to say 'retire because of this, retire because of that' but what they don't realise is we're members of a rare generation of entertaining British heavyweight boxers that are coming to the end of our careers.

"I love boxing and I'll fight anyone. Be grateful that you have guys like me around because when we're gone, there will be a long drought in the heavyweight division."

Johnny Fisher called for the return of Whyte last week, insisting that there is a 'good chance' the fight could happen in the near future.

Whyte readily accepted the verbal challenge and was watching from ringside as Fisher battled to a majority decision victory over Michael Pirotton at the Copper Box Arena last weekend.

"Credit to Johnny Fisher, because he's a big lump, he hasn't had time to learn a lot, but he's got a lot of courage, he's got a lot of heart, he's a big puncher and he's brave," said Whyte, who is open to facing Fisher in November or December this year.

"He's a bit frantic and that, but he's very brave and he's a big guy who punches hard. When the fight gets tough, he keeps trying and he keeps coming back.

"You can never overlook that but let's be honest, I will knock Johnny Fisher out, simple as that."

Whyte was joined by manager Michael Ofo, who says the fight has already been verbally accepted by Fisher's team and is hopeful it can be finalised.

"The fight was agreed in principle following Fisher's win on Saturday night with a handshake between me and Fisher's manager Adam Morallee," said Ofo.

"I was unsure whether Fisher and his management would take the fight, in spite of Fisher having called Dillian out, so I called Adam over and asked him. He immediately responded: 'Absolutely. Let's do it next!'

"It would be a huge all-British clash and a massive event for London. So, let's stop talking and get it on!"

articles.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua expected to go head to head at press conference in London on Wednesday
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are expected to go head to head for the first time since their all-British blockbuster fight was confirmed last Thursday; the pair are set to fight on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium
articles.body:
The British heavyweight rivals are set to go head-to-head for the first time since their blockbuster heavyweight fight was finally confirmed last week at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11.

Hearn had told Sky Sports over the weekend that "nothing was confirmed for next week, press conference-wise", and added: "with regards to are we expecting to be there, there wouldn't be one without us."

But Fury and Joshua will now trade words in front of the cameras and have a pre-fight face-off at British Airways ARC at the Olympia after an agreement was reached ahead of this week's eagerly awaited media event.

Fury raised fresh doubts about the fight taking place on Saturday, insisting there was a 'one per cent' chance that he would face Joshua next.

Hearn had recently questioned whether Fury has enrolled in pre-fight drug testing, but Fury's manager has confirmed to Sky Sports that he has enrolled six days earlier than required.

Joshua, Hearn, Fury and his promoter Frank Warren are now all set to be in attendance in London.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown, in an interview with Goldstar Promotions , said: "One thing is for sure: the Gypsy King will be there [at Wednesday's press conference] - one million per cent."

He added: "We were asked very early on to fight in London, to fight at Wembley, we agreed. Then it got moved to New York, we agreed to that. Our first contract was in Ireland; we're now four down the line with Wales, and we've agreed to that. We've agreed to everything."

Speaking to the FurociTV YouTube channel, Fury had said at the weekend: "If you've got a guy that wants to fight, yeah, and you've got a guy that doesn't want to fight, then how are you going to make that fight happen?

"I've had nearly 40 professional fights, yeah, and I've been on top of this game for over a decade, right? How did I manage to fight all these people before you, all these champions, yeah, for all these titles that there is in boxing, but, yeah, every time it comes to fighting [Joshua]... it never happens.

But Joshua and Fury are now going to press ahead with their media obligations for a fight that will reportedly have the WBA 'super' heavyweight title at stake.

"I've just seen today that it's for the WBA world heavyweight title as well, so that's another little bit of incentive," Fury said in his interview.

"Whoever wins this one will become three-time heavyweight champion. So that's another incentive to win."

articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense sometió a Sedriques Dumas en el primer asalto este pasado sábado para debutar por todo lo alto en la UFC
articles.body: Luis Hernandez (9-0) ha entrado por la puerta grande en la UFC en unas últimas semanas en las que se ha convertido en todo un ídolo de masas por lo que ha hecho tanto dentro como fuera del octágono. El peleador estadounidense, que también es policía de Miami-Dade y comparte agencia con Ilia Topuria, consiguió un contrato con la promotora el 15 de septiembre, y este pasado sábado aceptó un combate en corto aviso contra Sedrique Dumas para someterlo en el primer asalto y aumentar su popularidad. Hace unos días se pudo ver a Luis junto a Topuria en una foto donde posaban con una placa de policía, ya que Ilia ahora está viviendo en Miami y ambos forman parte de la agencia 'First Round Management'. Pocos días antes, el estadounidense se había hecho viral por su forma de celebrar la victoria ante Hugo Guillon en las Dana White's Contender Series después de someterle en el primer asalto, lo que le valió un contrato con la UFC. Cada vez que gana, Hernandez tiene preparados varios bailes diferentes y eso siempre llama la atención. Contra todo pronóstico, la UFC le llamo a falta de tres dias para el evento del sábado tras conocerse que el rival de Dumas se había lesionado, lo que generó uno de los combates más virales de los últimos tiempos. El motivo es que Sedriques cuenta con 15 arrestos policiales, por lo que todo el mundo quería ver el duelo entre ambos y las redes se llenaron de memes. 'The Stache' sometió a Dumas en menos de un minuto, y de nuevo dejó otra cantidad de bailes para el recuerdo. Lo cierto es que Luis ya era conocido antes de dar el salto a la UFC, ya que en junio de 2025 tuvo un fuerte altercado con Sean Strickland y Chris Curtis después de finalizar a su compañero de equipo Miles Hunsinger. Hernandez lo celebró dedicándoles un polémico baile, y ambos subieron a la jaula para echárselo en cara. De hecho, Strickland le lanzó dos puñetazos. Lo mejor de aquel beef es que Luis podría enfrentarse a Strickland en un futuro en la división de peso medio si sigue acumulando victorias. El duelo ante Dumas fue en peso semipesado al ser en corto aviso, y el propio peleador estadounidense ha adelantado que su objetivo es competir tanto en peso medio como en wélter, para poder tener más regularidad y aceptar los combates que más le interesen para su carrera. De momento ha finalizado a los nueve oponentes a los que se ha enfrentado, y a siete de ellos en el primer asalto. Si a esto se le suma su apariencia díscola, que es policía de Miami-Dade y que baila cada vez que gana, te queda un prospecto que podría convertirse en una futura superestrella si continúa haciendo las cosas de esta manera. Además, la UFC valora mucho que sus peleadores acepten combates en corto aviso para salvarles la papeleta, por lo que seguramente pronto vuelva a haber noticias sobre él.

articles.summary: Amid ongoing speculation about contractual disagreements, the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight scheduled for Dec. 11 looks to be back on.
articles.body:
Amid ongoing speculation about contractual disagreements, the Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight scheduled for Dec. 11 looks to be back on.

Per Ariel Helwani of Uncrowned.com, the heavyweight showdown "is back on track" after both sides went through a 48-hour negotiating period to work through the issues and a press conference is expected to be held on Wednesday.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

The long-rumored bout between Fury and Joshua was officially announced on Sept. 24.

However, the following day Mike Coppinger of Ring Magazine reported "issues" popped up that threatened to cancel the fight and potential replacement bouts were being discussed.

Per Sports Illustrated 's Chris Mannix , the primary issue is Dana White's involvement as a promoter of the fight.

Mannix noted Turki Alalshikh, a Saudi government official and co-founder of Zuffa Boxing with White, is "bankrolling" the fight and wants White involved with the promotion, but Joshua and his promoter, Eddie Hearn, "have a contract that says Zuffa can't" help promote the bout.

Hearn told iFL.tv (h/t ESPN's James Regan ) that White "cannot be involved with this fight promotion" and there is a "

Things between the two camps reached the point where Fury said on his YouTube channel over the weekend there was only a "one percent chance" the match with Joshua happens.

Assuming the fight happens as currently planned, it will mark the culmination of a years-long attempt to get Fury and Joshua in the ring together. They both signed a two-fight contract back in 2021, but no dates were announced at the time.

The deal fell apart in part because an arbitrator ruled in 2021 that Deontay Wilder was owed a third fight against Fury.

There have been various stop-and-start moments between Fury and Joshua in the years since, but this marks the first time an official date and venue have been announced for the matchup.

Wednesday's press conference is the next major hurdle on the way to the fight. All indications are it is set to take place in London at British Airways ARC to announce the bout.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: British heavyweights arrive in London for news conference
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua arrive in London for Wednesday’s launch news conference, with their December fight now expected to take place as scheduled.
articles.body:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua have both arrived in London before Wednesday's launch news conference for their fight.

It appears the all-British heavyweight contest - more than a decade in the making - remains on for 11 December at Cardiff's Principality Stadium following several days of uncertainty.

Fury, 38, has travelled back from the United States, where he had been at Walt Disney World Resort with his family, while Joshua, 36, has flown in from his training camp in Dubai.

Fury-Joshua was officially announced on Thursday by Saudi powerbroker Turki Alalshikh, but doubts emerged 24 hours later amid a dispute over the role of UFC chief Dana White in the promotion.

Broadcaster Netflix said Alalshikh's The Ring and White would collaborate to promote the event, but Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn said his fighter's contract prevented White from having a promotional role.

White said on Saturday night he did not know whether the fight - or Wednesday's news conference - would happen. BBC Sport now understands he will not attend the launch.

A further potential hurdle emerged late on Monday over Fury's enrolment in the Voluntary Anti-Doping Association (Vada) testing programme.

Fury's manager Spencer Brown has since said Fury is now enrolled with Vada, appearing to resolve another issue before the launch.

Fury and Joshua have never fought despite several previous attempts to make the all-British contest.

Wednesday's event at the British Airways ARC in Olympia will be the first time the pair have come face-to-face since the fight was officially announced, with a limited number of tickets also being made available to the public.

Analysis - can Wednesday reset the chaotic Fury-Joshua narrative?

There was at least something reassuring about seeing both men step out of cars in London on Tuesday, ready for Wednesday's launch.

But a Fury-Joshua fight being 'on' has now been announced so many times it is hard to keep count.

And that is part of the problem. We have been here before and there is no way to dress up the past few days as anything other than a desperately poor look for boxing.

The majority of supporters felt Fury-Joshua had arrived too late, with both men now former champions and far from the peak of their powers.

Yet within 48 hours of the long-awaited announcement, even some of those still excited by the contest had been turned into cynics.

Instead of discussing how Fury and Joshua match up, the conversation became about promoters, contractual clauses, competing egos and whether the fight would happen at all.

That is remarkable for a shared purse reported to be worth close to $200m (£151m), backed by some of the most powerful figures in the sport.

Hearn has alleged contractual terms around White's involvement have not been adhered to. White has publicly attacked Hearn. Fury accused Joshua's camp of trying to pull out.

All of it created unnecessary uncertainty around a fight boxing has spent years failing to deliver.

With all that said, Wednesday offers an opportunity to change the mood quickly.

If Fury and Joshua both walk on stage and produce the kind of fireworks their rivalry had long-promised, some - though not all - of the noise of the past few days could fade.

articles.title: Nuevo mensaje de Topuria: "De vuelta a la oficina"
articles.standfirst: 'El Matador' ha compartido varias fotos entrenando y preparando su regreso tras su derrota ante Justin Gaethje
articles.summary: 'El Matador' ha compartido varias fotos entrenando y preparando su regreso tras su derrota ante Justin Gaethje
articles.body: Ilia Topuria ha subido una nueva publicación en Instagram donde ha mostrado que está de vuelta en el gimnasio y preparando su regreso tras su dura derrota ante Justin Gaethje en el UFC Casa Blanca. Con un escueto mensaje, 'El Matador' ha dejado claro que quiere volver más fuerte que nunca, puliendo su boxeo y planificando quién será su siguiente rival. Gaethje tiene decidido no darle la revancha a Topuria de manera inminente, por lo que la opción más probable y mediática puede que sea la de Paddy Pimblett por todo lo que significaría un cruce entre ambos. Sin embargo, no se espera a Ilia de vuelta hasta 2027, por lo que todo irá poco a poco. De momento, su mensaje es claro: "De vuelta a la oficina". El peleador hispanogeorgiano se tomó unas semanas de descanso tras su derrota ante Gaethje para sanar tanto física como mentalmente. Topuria acabó la pelea con fracturas en el pie, la nariz y los dos orbitales, pero desde hace unas semanas ya está de vuelta en el gimnasio con el claro objetivo de vengar su único traspiés profesional. Además, ya se ha confirmado que Aleksandre Topuria regresará al octágono el próximo 21 de noviembre en el UFC Qatar ante Santiago Luna, por lo que se espera que 'El Matador' haga junto a su hermano mayor el campamento con tal de que llegue en la mejor forma posible. Una vez se supere esa misión, será momento de fijar una fecha y un rival para él. Lo normal es que Topuria regrese en una cartelera numerada en el primer trimestre del 2027, aunque tampoco sería nada descabellado pensar en el posible evento numerado que se celebre en abril en Miami como sucede cada año. Ahora que Ilia reside allí, sería la fecha perfecta para su vuelta una vez hayan sanado las heridas tras perder el cinturón ante Gaethje. De momento, la mejor noticia es que ha vuelto a hacer lo que mejor sabe, por lo que su vuelta está cada vez más cerca.

articles.title: Justin Gaethje siembra la duda y no deja claro si volverá a pelear
articles.standfirst: El peleador estadounidense afirma que ya no tiene que demostrar nada a nadie, por lo que podría retirarse sin defender el cinturón de peso ligero
articles.summary: El peleador estadounidense afirma que ya no tiene que demostrar nada a nadie, por lo que podría retirarse sin defender el cinturón de peso ligero
articles.body: El futuro de Justin Gaethje en la UFC es una completa incógnita. Tras derrotar a Ilia Topuria el pasado 14 de junio en el UFC Casa Blanca y cumplir su sueño de ser campeón indiscutido de peso ligero, el estadounidense ha dejado caer que podría retirarse sin llegar a defender el cinturón. A pesar de que tiene varios oponentes sobre la mesa existe la posibilidad de que no vuelva a subirse al octágono, ya que según afirma no tiene nada que demostrar a nadie. Topuria tiene ganas de vengarse de su única derrota profesional, pero el peleador estadounidense no está muy por la labor, ya que cree que 'El Matador' no hizo méritos suficientes para ello. Por otro lado está la posibilidad de un combate entre Gaethje y Arman Tsarukyan, que es la opción más real según afirma el propio Justin. Sin embargo, también cabe la posibilidad de que deje el cinturón vacante y ponga fin a su carrera a sus 37 años. Gaethje podría haber dicho adiós a lo grande en la Casa Blanca, en el mayor escenario posible y ante su gente, pero está disfrutando de estos meses como campeón y todavía no tiene claro cuál será su siguiente paso. "Todo el mundo me dice: 'pelea contra Arman'. Tengo lesiones que debo tratar, aún no he tomado una decisión. Tengo 37 años, he disputado 40 combates... No lo sé, no necesito volver a pelear", confesó en 'Flagrant Podcast'. Lo cierto es que no es la primera vez que Gaethje amaga con la retirada, ya que a finales de 2025 también amenazó con retirarse si la UFC no le daba una oportunidad por el cinturón indiscutido. Finalmente tuvo que conformarse con pelear por el cinturón interino contra Paddy Pimblett, al que pasó por encima para unificar más tarde los cinturones ante Topuria de manera exitosa. Gaethje también ha dicho que su siguiente derrota supondrá el fin de su carrera, teoría que cobra fuerza ahora que ha cumplido todos sus objetivos. Por tanto, en caso de que no se retire se espera que le queden como mucho una o dos peleas más después de años y años dando espectáculo. Estas declaraciones también se pueden entender como un intento de negociar su siguiente salario, ya que querrá cobrar el máximo dinero posible en sus últimos combates en la UFC. Ahora que es campeón, ese sueldo subirá notablemente, pero seguramente su intención y la de Ali Abdelaziz -su mánager- sea sacar el mayor partido posible a su siguiente aparición. Las opciones más viables ahora mismo son la retirada que él mismo menciona, o un combate contra Arman Tsarukyan, con la posible revancha contra Topuria cada vez más lejos.

articles.title: Parveen Hooda’s redemption fight: From 22-month ban and lost medal to Asian Games final
articles.summary: As Parveen Hooda unleashes fury inside the ring, she is fighting battles far beyond it. The Rohtak boxer is punching at more than an opponent now.
articles.body: As Parveen Hooda unleashes fury inside the ring, she is fighting battles far beyond it. The Rohtak boxer is punching at more than an opponent now. Every counter carries the weight of a medal taken away, an Olympic dream that vanished and a family waiting for relief.The road here has been paved with setbacks, sacrifice and a hunger for redemption.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThree years ago, Parveen won bronze at the Hangzhou Games. Then came the whereabouts failure, a 22-month suspension and the stripping of her medal. The Paris Olympics slipped away. Her Glasgow CWG return in July-August ended in a quarterfinal defeat.Now, in Aichi-Nagoya, she has fought her way back to the final, beating China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal.A silver is assured. But Parveen is not looking back. She wants gold and full redemption.Her fight has always extended beyond the ring. Her father, Lakhpat Hooda, has been battling cancer for four years and is also a heart patient. Her mother, Neelam Devi, sells buffalo milk to keep the household running, while Parveen’s 20-year-old younger brother is studying.An ITBP Assistant Sub-Inspector, Parveen has become the family’s principal breadwinner.“Parveen takes care of every need of the family,” her childhood coach Sudhir Hooda told TOI. “She has been funding her father’s medical treatment with cash awards from boxing and her ITBP income.”Hooda first saw Parveen in April 2010. She was in Class 5, barely 22kg, and came from a family that struggled to afford boxing nutrition.“I became the village sarpanch and opened an academy in Rohtak to keep youngsters away from drugs and crime, offering 80 children free coaching, milk and diet. Parveen was one of the brightest.”Ankush Panghal provided another headline, stunning Uzbekistan’s Fazliddin Erkinboev 4-1 in the 80kg semifinal.After dropping the opening round, Ankush changed gears, attacked the body and dominated the finish. He is India’s first male Asian Games finalist since Amit Panghal in 2018.Narender Berwal secured bronze after a 0-5 loss to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the +90kg semifinal. articles.body: El boxeador Arturo 'Lobito' Torres murió con 26 años después de permanecer ingresado una semana en el hospital en coma inducido. El púgil mexicano fue ingresado tras perder el conocimiento durante un combate que perdió por KO técnico ante Gilberto 'Torito' García el 19 de septiembre en Mexicali (Baja California). Su equipo técnico lo llevó inmediatamente al Hospital General de Mexicali, donde los médicos le diagnosticaron un coágulo cerebral, por lo que fue sometido a una operación que, en un primer momento, había resultado satisfactoria. articles.title: Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua press conference: 'Fury will try every trick in the book to get to AJ'
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are expected to go head to head for the first time at a at press conference in London on Wednesday; the British rivals are due to fight on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in a long-anticipated heavyweight clash
articles.body:
I think the press conference will be important.

The psychological, mental aspect of boxing is huge. It's an individual sport - one on one - so if you can get into the other guy's head and help put him in a negative headspace, you're halfway there.

Confidence is key. And if someone's struggling with confidence, if you can put some seeds of doubt in their mind, that's a real benefit to you.

There's a lot on the line. A lot of people involved, a lot of money, a lot of pride, a lot of ego, so there's already cracks appearing left, right and centre.

Fury will certainly be trying every trick in the book.

There will be people there who will try and control things as best they can, trying to make sure that nothing physical happens. But I'd expect Fury to be animated.

Joshua less so. I wouldn't have said that the psychological warfare was as big a part of AJ's game as it is Fury's. I don't think he's as well versed in it.

But sometimes not engaging can be good, it can sort of give you the edge - like Carl Froch the second time round with George Groves.

I think he realised that for the first fight he wasted so much energy on things and fell into the traps that George was setting.

I think was it Michael Corleone [in The Godfather III] who said, "Never hate your enemies, it affects your judgment". And I think, certainly with Froch the first time round, that was a factor.

Ahead of the second fight, he just chose to disengage. So maybe AJ will do similar and choose to not get involved?

I think we'll get there. I think the fight will go ahead, but I do think there'll be some twists and turns and bumps in the road on the way.

articles.summary: India’s strong boxing campaign at the Asian Games has given the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) confidence ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
articles.body: India’s strong boxing campaign at the Asian Games has given the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) confidence ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.BFI president Ajay Singh praised the Indian boxers after the team secured six medals from 11 events, including three finalists. He said the Asian Games field is close to what boxers face at the Olympics.Six medals from 11 eventsIndia added three more bronze medals on Wednesday through Priya Ghanghas, Narender and Kapil Pokhariya, who lost their respective semifinal bouts.Lovlina Borgohain, Ankush Dahiya and Parveen Hooda have already reached their respective finals and will fight for gold.“We've got six medals in this Asian Games out of 11 events. Last time we got four medals out of 13 events that were held. So we've done considerably better than the last time,” Singh said.He also pointed out that three Indian boxers reaching the finals was a big achievement given the quality of competition at the Asian Games.“The fact that three boxers are in the finals now, I think, is an incredible achievement given that the Asian Games for boxing is very similar to the Olympics,” he said.‘Performance can be replicated at Olympics’Singh believes the performance in the Asian Games can give a clear indication of what India can achieve at the Olympics.“All the top countries in the world are in the Asian Games. So whatever performance we are doing here, it's very possible that this will be replicated in the Olympics,” he said.“So getting six medals, out of which three are now in the finals, is an incredible achievement. articles.title: Briton George Staines claims 61-second win to earn UFC contract
articles.summary: Britain's George Staines stops Loai Abushaar in stunning fashion to earn a UFC contract in Dana White's Contender Series.
articles.body:
Britain's George Staines stopped Loai Abushaar in stunning fashion to earn a UFC contract in Dana White's Contender Series.

Staines, 26, took just 61 seconds to rubberstamp his spot in MMA's leading promotion.

The lightweight, who hails from Hull but trains alongside UFC star Paddy Pimblett in Liverpool, slammed Abushaar to the floor before finishing with ground-and-pound.

He was one of four fighters to be handed a contract and was cheered on by Pimblett and fellow UFC fighter Luke Riley as he closed out the show in Las Vegas.

"George, you were up against a massive guy at 155lb and you absolutely destroyed him," UFC president Dana White said.

"It was one of the greatest finishes ever, you made it look easy - congratulations and welcome to the UFC."

Victory extended Staines' perfect professional record to 11 victories, having previously competed under the banner of Oktagon and Cage Warriors.

articles.title: Antonio Collado y la recompensa del boxeador: "Esta es la pelea que le había pedido a Dios"
articles.standfirst: El joven púgil disputa el título Europeo Silver contra su compatriota Brian Peláez en una velada imperdible
articles.summary: El joven púgil disputa el título Europeo Silver contra su compatriota Brian Peláez en una velada imperdible
articles.body: Antonio Collado (23-3, 4 KOs) sigue dando pasos adelante en su carrera y este sábado formará parte de la que posiblemente sea la velada del año en España, en la que se disputarán dos Campeonatos de Europa absolutos (Navarro vs. Guinea y Alhambra vs. Messaoudi) y un EBU Silver, que es la pelea que lo involucra a él. El púgil de Quintanar de la Orden se enfrenta a Brian Peláez (18-8-2, 3 KOs) por el segundo título continental en importancia, en un duelo que será una revancha del Campeonato de España del peso ligero que ambos se disputaron en 2023 y que se llevó Collado por decisión unánime. Han pasado más de dos años de aquello y Antonio ha disputado nada menos que 15 peleas más. Un camino de mucho esfuerzo recorrido para seguir adquiriendo la experiencia que lo llevara a las peleas con las que había soñado desde que se puso unos guantes. ¿Nervioso? “No, no estoy nervioso. Estoy en el momento en el que sabes que si aparecen esos nervios son buenos. Ahora no pienso en otra cosa que no sea acabar con las manos en alto, pero que tengo que afrontar esto con la cabeza fría. Hay confianza, pero sin confiarme”, explica Collado. Bajo ningún concepto, el joven entrenado por Víctor del Toro en Rivas Vaciamadrid quiere dejar escapar esta oportunidad. “Esta pelea ha sido algo que le he pedido a Dios desde que me puse los guantes por primera vez, estoy con todo el hambre del mundo. Es el billete de oro al título absoluto de Europa”, comenta Collado, que apostilla: “Pero vayamos paso a paso”. Según expresa Antonio, “cada vez soy un boxeador más metódico y perfeccionista. Vamos a ver a un Antonio sin dudas. Durante mi carrera me he caído y me he levantado para llegar hasta donde estoy”. Sobre su preparación, Collado es la escuela del ‘no hay dolor’ de Rocky Balboa: “Para mí este campamento no ha sido sacrificado porque era algo que le pedía a Dios. Sarna con gusto no pica. Esto es por lo que vivo”, detalla el joven peso ligero español. Aunque hubo algún sinsabor a lo largo de estos años de carrera, Collado sólo siente agradecimiento al deporte que eligió como modo de vida: “El boxeo me está dando más de lo que esperaba y ahora me regala una de esas noches con las que yo soñaba. Empecé en un garaje yo solo dando golpes a un saco y ya me sentía realizado, era feliz sin necesidad de recibir aplausos”. Ahora forma parte de algo grande, de un “veladón que ha organizado la promotora JHM y les agradezco que hayan contado con nosotros”. Sobre su rival, Brian Peláez, el de Quintanar habla con respeto: “Es un magnífico boxeador al que he visto desde que yo era amateur. Para mí esta pelea no es un revancha, es un combate desde cero. Lo que pasó hace tres años ya es historia, somos personas distintas cuyo boxeo ha seguido evolucionado”. El trabajo –“muy duro”, recalca Antonio- ya está hecho y ahora toca velar armas y dar el peso: “Hemos implementado más descanso estas dos últimas semanas para llegar en el punto óptimo y estoy cumpliendo con los pesajes”.

articles.title: Who is Wang Cong? Chinese UFC star set to compete at UFC 332 for vacant flyweight title against Natalia Silva
articles.summary: Wang Cong is one of the most experienced strikers in the UFC women’s flyweight division.
articles.body: Wang Cong is one of the most experienced strikers in the UFC women’s flyweight division. The Chinese fighter has built a strong combat sports career across Sanda, kickboxing, boxing and mixed martial arts. Now, she is preparing for the biggest fight of her MMA career.Cong will face Natalia Silva for the vacant UFC Women’s Flyweight Championship at UFC 332 on October 3 in Salt Lake City. The opportunity came after Valentina Shevchenko vacated the title because of an injury. Cong believes her four-fight winning streak and availability made her the natural choice.Who is Wang Cong? Wang Cong was born on May 15, 1992, in Dalian, Liaoning, China. She is 34 years old and competes at 125 pounds in the UFC flyweight division. She is known by the nickname “The Joker” and trains with Team Alpha Male.Cong has a professional MMA record of 10-1. She also has a decorated background in Sanda and kickboxing. She won gold in Sanda at the 2013 World Wushu Championships and the 2014 Asian Games. She also won silver in amateur boxing at the 2019 World Championships.Her kickboxing career includes a major victory over Valentina Shevchenko. Cong defeated Shevchenko by unanimous decision at Kunlun Fight 33 in October 2015. The victory also saw her win the Kunlun Fight Women’s Lightweight Championship.Cong later moved into MMA and continued to build her record. She earned a UFC contract after submitting Paula Luna at Road to UFC in May 2024.Her UFC debut came against Victoria Leonardo in August 2024. Cong stopped Leonardo with punches in just 62 seconds and received a Performance of the Night bonus.She suffered the first loss of her professional MMA career against Gabriella Fernandes in November 2024. However, Cong quickly bounced back.She then defeated Bruna Brasil, Ariane da Silva, Eduarda Moura and Tracy Cortez. Her win over Cortez at UFC 329 in July 2026 extended her winning streak to four fights. That run helped put her in position for the biggest opportunity of her career.Cong was ranked sixth in the flyweight division when the title fight was announced. Some questioned why she was selected ahead of other contenders. However, Cong said the situation within the division made the decision understandable.“I’m not surprised. Because how the rankings go either has a fight booked or they just fought. I’m on a four fight win streak and I think it’s my time”, Cong told MMA Fighting.Top contenders including Alexa Grasso and Manon Fiorot had recently fought each other, while other fighters such as Erin Blanchfield were also in contention. Cong, meanwhile, was available and coming off four straight victories.The matchup with Silva is also expected to be a battle between two skilled strikers. Cong believes controlling the pace will be crucial when they meet inside the Delta Center.The winner of Cong vs. Silva will leave UFC 332 as the new UFC Women’s Flyweight Champion. articles.body:
Fireworks have already started ahead of the highly anticipated showdown between heavyweight legends Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

During Wednesday's pre-fight press conference, Fury had a bold prediction for how the Dec. 11 showdown will play out.

"I can tell you the strategy that I'm gonna impose, because that's what I do," Fury said. "I tell you what I'm gonna do, I'm gonna come out and I'm gonna blast him out of there. It will be 'gunfight at the O.K. Corral.' And it will be the best man's gonna win, because I ain't gonna run away, I'm not gonna box, I'm gonna throw down. And from what I'm seeing, I'm gonna catch him, and when I do, it's gonna be curtains. And that's it."

NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 4 🏈

For his part, Joshua seemed unfazed as he laughed off Fury's fiery claims, and he said he's extra motivated to come out victorious when they meet at Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales.

"We love it. This is the energy that we want. This is a fight. There's nothing else that I expect from this man than to say he's gonna render me unconscious and do everything he can to stick me to the canvas," Joshua said. "But this is what's gonna keep me running. This is what's gonna keep me sparring. This is what's gonna make me do those extra rounds in the gym, because I want to perform to prove to myself that what he says is not possible, and for everyone that's coming out to support me, to live up to the expectations that they have of me."

The fight between Joshua and Fury has been over a decade in the making, so fans will be excited to see them finally settle their differences in the ring later this year.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua: British rivals trade taunts about negotiations for long-awaited fight at first press conference in London
articles.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally settle their rivalry in a British heavyweight blockbuster at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Friday December 11; Fury and Joshua both traded taunts at their first press conference in London; The British duo then shared a face-off
articles.body:
The British heavyweight rivals finally went head to head in front of the cameras and traded a few jibes about the protracted talks that have repeatedly delayed their long-awaited fight.

Fury and Joshua will share the ring at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Friday December 11 and both men offered their own version of why the boxing world was made to wait again for this fight.

"In the build-up to this fight, Eddie and AJ were talking about landlords and being the boss and being the Guvnor and the rent man and all that," said Fury.

"When I look behind me, I only see one Don and that's Fury vs AJ. Now you've come to get the rent and I ain't f****** paying, because I'm number one.

"I don't make a big thing about all that, but we're going to walk out seeing Tyson Fury versus his opponent Anthony Joshua - an old dosser who works for me."

Joshua quickly interjected by saying: "I got a phone call the other night and they said 'do you mind if Fury's name goes first, because he's unwilling to sign unless he does'."

But Fury was determined to have the final word and replied:" Behind the scenes, you've been crying like little girls over A-sides and B-sides. I want this, I want that!

"You have tried everything to get out of this fight, every move in the book. And now I've checkmated you!"

When asked about their fight tactics, Fury insists he will adopt an ultra-aggressive approach as he seeks a swift knockout.

"I'm going to come out and I'm going to blast him out there," said Fury.

"It will gunfight at the O.K. Corral and the best man is going to win, because I'm not going to run way and I'm not going to box. I'm going to throw down!

"From what I'm seeing, I'm going to catch him and - when I do - it's going to be curtains."

But Joshua welcomed this pre-fight prediction from Fury, admitting he will use it as motivation to pull off his own momentous victory.

"This is the energy that we want, said Joshua.

"There's nothing else I'd expect from this man than him to say he's going to render me unconscious and do everything he can to stick me to the canvas.

"This is what is going to keep me running, this what is going to keep me sparring and this is going to keep me doing those extra rounds in the gym."

The two former unified champions will meet in the closing chapters of their career, with Fury 38 years-old and Joshua is 36.

But Fury has dismissed suggestions that the fight has lost some of its significance.

"It has been 10 years in the making," he said.

"The rise has been phenomenal for both fighters - we've both had our ups and down - and we arrive at this moment.

"Is it too late? Is it f*** too late. It's the icing on the cake of two great careers, to throw down in front of 80,000 people, and may the best man win.

A former Olympics gold medallist, Joshua then emerged as an world heavyweight champion and he believes all his previous fights have prepared him for this moment.

"People have their views and views are respected, but that's their opinion," he said.

"I can only listen to myself and nobody knows more about boxing than me. I'm great, I'm good.

"I've been from gym to gym and been from coach to coach and I can honestly say I've learned so much.

"I'm going to take everything I've learned into this fight."

articles.title: Boxing stock watch: September’s biggest winners and losers, as Ryan Garcia rises and Dana White stumbles
articles.summary: Who won and lost boxing’s month of September? Let's break it all down.
articles.body:
September is over, Billie Joe Armstrong has woken from his slumber, and we have some winners and losers to anoint across the boxing month.

Across 30 days of action inside and outside of the ring, we witnessed Katie Taylor's retirement party , 265 seconds of Garcia vs. Benn , and Dana White trying to elbow his way to the top table of the recently announced "Battle of Britain" between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

But where do they sit on our list? Keep scrolling to find out.

The "Emerald Isle's" darling waved goodbye to boxing on her own terms in September, headlining an emotional evening of action inside Dublin's historic Croke Park.

Taylor got the nod over France's Flora Pili to capture the undisputed world super lightweight titles in her farewell fight, 27 professional bouts into a historic career.

It was a truly remarkable setting for one of Ireland's most revered athletes.

Addressing the buoyant crowd post-fight, she said: "Croke Park! We did it! I don't know of any other country that ​would sell 80,000 tickets. The people of Ireland gave me a dream end to a dream career. Nothing can top this. This was definitely the highlight of my whole career."

There's an argument to suggest that Ryan Garcia recorded the biggest win of his career in September.

All boxing eyes were on his lightweight clash with Conor Benn, and Garcia blew his adversary away inside an electric two rounds.

The keys to Garcia becoming the new "face" of boxing are within reach. If he's able to lock down headline events on Mexican holidays, keep himself out of trouble and lure the biggest names into world title fights, then there is no limit to Garcia's superstardom.

"King Ry" wants to stay active and is open to fighting again before the end of the year. And the 28-year-old could well find himself in the conversation for Fighter of the Year honors if he can make it to three wins in 2026, having first claimed the WBC welterweight world title against Mario Barrios before successfully defending it against Benn.

With the popularity and eyeballs that Garcia brings to fight nights, he won't be short for suitors as opponents.

Eddie Hearn has been smiling like a Cheshire cat in September.

First, he basked in the love of a nation after Katie Taylor's historic night at Croke Park. Then he dug in his heels and got Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua to British shores, sticking two fingers up in the process to everyone on the other side of the deal who wanted Madison Square Garden to host the heavyweight blockbuster.

Oh, and third, let's not forget the heavy dose of schadenfreude he experienced as he witnessed his former client turned enemy, Conor Benn, lose in such a comprehensive style to Ryan Garcia.

Sure, Hearn spends more hours in front of a camera than he does asleep across a normal 24-hour day, but even with his continued attempts to control the boxing narrative, it's hard not to paint the Matchroom mogul as a big winner in September.

The first time was so nice … he had to do it twice.

Ten months after beating Japanese superstar Tenshin Nasukawa for the WBC bantamweight title, Takuma Inoue did it again in September , again by unanimous decision, and again inside Tokyo's Toyota Arena.

But the sailing wasn't as smooth this time around.

Inoue, 30, had to climb off the canvas in the seventh round en route to a narrow decision on the scorecards, all but ending — for now — Nasukawa's ambitions to challenge Takuma's older brother, Naoya Inoue, in what would be a Japanese superfight.

But Inoue has ambitions of his own. With just the WBC title to his name, the 118-pounder made it clear post-fight where he sees his immediate future by stating: "I'm not satisfied with just one belt, I want to collect more."

The Pat Brown bandwagon gained more momentum in September, as the likable and well-followed Mancunian bulldozed his way to the British cruiserweight title.

Brown, 26, moved to a pretty green 7-0 (7 KOs) against John Hedges inside the Co-op Live, inflicting Ricky Hatton-inspired body shots onto the big frame of Hedges, closing the argument in the sixth round.

Brown's ceiling is extremely high in the cruiserweight division, but so is the talent above him. His promotor, Eddie Hearn, claimed post-fight that his charge will "dismantle [Jai] Opetaia" if they fight, saying that they want a meeting with the Australian world champion "next year."

But Hearn and Team Brown may be wise to learn the lessons that his compatriot Moses Itauma learned at the end of August. Time is on the side of the "Bomber," and his journey will be worth keeping a very close eye on.

Conor Benn lasted just a round and a half against Ryan Garcia in a failed attempt to land the WBC lightweight world championship.

It was a bit of a reality check under the Las Vegas lights for the plucky Briton, who was stopped by the referee after an unanswered assault on the ropes by Garcia, having previously tasted the canvas after a vicious right hand sent him tumbling.

Where Benn, 30, goes from here is anyone's guess.

He now faces the sharper end of the double-edged sword after skipping British and European level opposition in favor of chasing the bigger paydays and brighter lights.

Another crack at lightweight gold? Middleweight? Super middleweight? A rubber match with family rival Chris Eubank Jr.?

He's still a big name in the sport, but after blowing millions on the signature of "The "Destroyer," Zuffa Boxing might be at a loss for how to successfully — and, more importantly, lucratively — match him over the next couple of years.

Andy Ruiz Jr's return to the ring after a two-year layoff ended in defeat in September , but the loss may not even be the most concerning part.

It's more that the victor of this heavyweight fight, Damian Knyba, was so heavily fancied across the sport's landscape as an underdog heading into this fight, underlining the lack of belief and relative interest that the boxing world has left for Ruiz.

Ruiz dropped a unanimous decision loss to the Polish-born New Yorker, handing the former unified heavyweight world champion the third loss of his professional career.

Ruiz has vowed to continue in the sport and, indicative of his new perceived level, has since been called out by a man who you'll read a little more about if you scroll down: Dave Allen.

Dana White's standing in the announced Dec. 11 heavyweight fight between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua unraveled in 17 minutes of questioning in September .

White has repeatedly dubbed himself as one of the biggest and most important players involved in getting this long-awaited fight over the line, but in the post-fight press conference of Zuffa Boxing's latest event, the UFC CEO became increasingly frustrated with journalists as he cracked under the lightest of pressure.

It turns out White doesn't know much about Dec. 11.

"We'll see how this thing plays out" was his repeated attempt to move the scrutiny on, but the optics weren't good for the multi-millionaire who is used to getting things his own way.

In reality, White has no business sticking his nose in the promotion of this fight. Netflix clearly wants him and TKO involved to some capacity, but at the expense of breaching contracts and the fight falling out of bed, again? I doubt it.

Thomas Carty didn't appear to fancy life as a heavyweight boxer in September.

Eighty-two seconds into his shift inside Dublin's Croke Park on the Taylor-Pili undercard, and the 30-year-old southpaw appeared to jump out of the ring and clock off from his heavyweight bout with British journeyman/comedian Dave Allen.

OK, the Dubliner did take a clubbing blow to the back of the head from Allen, but you'll need to come at me with a multitude of physics degrees and letters after your surname to convince me that what followed was a natural reaction to such an event.

Carty, channelling Iyo Sky's suicide dive, went spilling into the laps of photographers and ringside dignitaries, giving Dave Allen a no-contest on his record, but more importantly, the chance to headline Wrestlemania 43. That's how it works, right?

Most jokes aside, thankfully , Carty wasn't seriously injured. Allen is still lobbying for a win to appear on his record, but in all honesty, this one is probably worth filing in the "did that fight actually happen?" document.

If it walks like a duck, looks like a duck and quacks like a duck, then, unfortunately, it's probably a duck.

And that's the accusation that former WBO super middleweight world champion Hamzah Sheeraz had to stand up to in September, after he dropped his world title rather than facing the mandated challenge of Janibek Alimkhanuly .

Now granted, Janibek's position as the mandatory challenger for this 168-pound title is extremely controversial. Last December, the Kazakh returned a positive test for the banned substance meldonium, resulting in a 12-month ban from the WBO.

Sheeraz has made his feelings known on the situation, stating on "The Ariel Helwani Show" that, "I think what the WBO has done here is disgraceful to the sport of boxing," which is fine, but the contradiction lies in the number of times Sheeraz has called for a fight with Saul "Canelo" Alvarez — another fighter who has a history of failed drugs tests.

Janibek is a dangerous fighter. Sheeraz — rightly or wrongly — weighed up the pros and cons of mixing it with the Kazakh and has opted for an easier route in the pro game under the protected wing of Turki Alalshikh.
